title: TypeScript SDK: protocol adaptor for resumable streams and AsyncIterator/Web Stream handshake
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Developers building against the TS SDK increasingly need ergonomic conversion between AsyncIterator and Web Streams while also supporting robust resume semantics for long-running generations, multi-consumer handoff, and client reconnects. Existing adapters in the codebase cover basic conversion but do not expose an opinionated resumption protocol that embeds lightweight checkpoints and enables deterministic replay from a checkpoint token.

Goal: Implement a protocol adaptor in the TS SDK that: 1) provides a safe, well-typed bridge between ReadableStream and AsyncIterator across Node/Deno/Browser runtimes, 2) exposes a compact resumption token API that can be persisted and supplied to reconnects, and 3) integrates with the SDK's retry and fallback policies to allow transparent retry with resume instead of full restart where possible.

Design summary: The adaptor has two primary pieces: (A) a runtime-agnostic bridge that converts between ReadableStream<T> and AsyncIterator<T> while preserving backpressure and cancellation semantics, and (B) a small resumption protocol layered on top that emits periodic checkpoint frames (every N tokens or bytes) and exposes getResumeToken() on the returned iterator.

API surface (proposed):
- createProtocolStream<T>(source: ReadableStream<T> | AsyncIterable<T>, opts?: { checkpointInterval?: number; encoding?: 'utf8' | 'base64'; onResume?: (meta) => void; }): { iterator: AsyncIterable<T>; stream?: ReadableStream<T>; getResumeToken: () => string | null; resumeWith: (token: string) => Promise<void> }

- Checkpoint token format: compact base64-encoded JSON: { v:1, seq: <number>, offset: <byte|token>, meta?: <string> }. Token must be opaque to consumers but small enough to store in localStorage/session.

Implementation notes:
- Use minimal runtime shims: prefer native ReadableStream in browsers, use web-streams-polyfill for Node <18 compatibility and Deno compatibility checks.
- Backpressure bridge: when converting ReadableStream -> AsyncIterator, drive the ReadableStreamDefaultReader.read() loop and yield values only when consumer requests next(). Use an internal queue with a bounded size to avoid memory blowup; expose options to tune queue length.
- Cancellation propagation: cancellation on iterator.return()/throw() must call reader.cancel() and flush pending checkpoints. Conversely, if underlying stream errors, propagate to iterator via throw().
- Resumption behavior: checkpoint frames are produced by SDK-side serialization of stable tokens (sequence number + small prefix of last bytes). On reconnect with resume token, the SDK will: validate token against a lightweight checksum, call the model endpoint with resume header x-rw-resume: <token>, and server/runtime will attempt to resume from aligned KV/cache offsets. If server cannot resume, server responses will include x-rw-resume-status: rejected and the SDK should fall back to full restart with best-effort deduplication.

Testing & compatibility:
- Unit tests for Node (native ReadableStream), Node with web-streams-polyfill, Deno, and browser.
- E2E: instrumented test that simulates mid-stream disconnect, then calls resumeWith(token) and asserts identical tail tokens produced and no duplication beyond prefix.
- Fuzz tests for malformed tokens and token replay attacks.

Operational considerations:
- Tokens are opaque and small; do not include PII.
- Documentation must include migration notes for existing consumers that use the older stream helpers.

Why this is different: the adaptor standardizes a simple resumption contract in the SDK (rather than leaving restart/resume semantics ad hoc in apps) and provides a single ergonomic entrypoint for both AsyncIterator and ReadableStream consumers across runtimes.
comments: 2026-03-10 - kickoff: initial design doc posted to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/ts-stream-protocol-adaptor (internal). Action: prototype bridge in a feature branch.

2026-03-11 - prototype: implemented basic ReadableStream -> AsyncIterator bridge in branch feat/stream-proto-adaptor. Added queue with default size 64. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4321 (WIP).
2026-03-11 - design feedback (PM): prefer token expiry metadata and explicit TTL policy. Added TTL to token shape and will add optional onExpire callback.

2026-03-12 - eng review: suggested making getResumeToken() idempotent and lightweight; Rajesh to add tiny checksum to avoid accidental invalid tokens. Also recommended adding a helper decodeResumeToken() in tests to validate internal fields without relying on opaque decode in production.

2026-03-12 - blocker noted: server-side resume header x-rw-resume needs infra support in runtime; created dependency ENG-27158 to coordinate with serving team. Temporary fallback planned (full restart) when header is missing.
2026-03-12 - next: add browser smoke tests, update docs/CHANGELOG, and add feature flag controlled rollout for beta users.
acceptance_criteria: API implemented and exported from @rw/sdk/streams with TypeScript types and docstrings.
Backpressure preserved: consumer await next() controls upstream read() calls and queue does not exceed configured limit under test.
Cancel/return semantics correctly propagate to underlying stream reader and pending checkpoint flush completes.
Resume token generated and accepted by server stub in E2E tests; resume path used when server indicates resume-available header.
Cross-runtime tests (Node native, Node polyfilled, Deno, Chrome) pass in CI.
Docs and migration guide published and linked from SDK README.
